# Results — Study 314 (Jackson-Hole) on the real SPY tape

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). An event study around the
**Friday keynote** of the Fed's late-August **Jackson Hole Economic Symposium**:
tag the trading session at each fixed offset from the speech and compare its return to
all other days. Tape: shared SPY daily total returns (`_cache/last_call_spy.parquet`),
1993-02-01 → 2026-06-11. As-of **2026-06-11**; match the fingerprint to confirm you hold
the same tape. The offline reproducible core and test-suite run on the deterministic
[`data.synthetic_world`](../jackson_hole/data.py) generator, never the network.*

## Data stamp

| Series | Window | Days | Fingerprint |
|---|---|--:|---|
| SPY daily total returns | 1993-02-01 → 2026-06-11 | 8,398 | `ffd9a70d0571` |
| Jackson Hole keynotes | 1993 → 2025 | **33 events** | one Friday speech per year |

## The drift profile around the keynote — every offset, all events

Event-day mean vs all other days, by session offset from the Friday speech (offset 0 =
the speech day; −1 = the day before; +1 = the day after). HAC = Newey-West t on the
event-day mean; Welch = t on the event-minus-rest difference. **n = 33 every row.**

| offset | event mean (bps) | diff vs rest (bps) | Welch *t* | HAC *t* | win-rate |
|---:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| −5 | −5.2 | −10.0 | −0.56 | −0.34 | 52% |
| −4 | −14.5 | −19.3 | −0.97 | −0.72 | 48% |
| −3 | −6.7 | −11.4 | −0.66 | −0.43 | 52% |
| −2 | +25.7 | +21.1 | +1.21 | +1.75 | 61% |
| **−1** | **−26.7** | **−31.6** | **−1.50** | **−1.07** | 36% |
| **0 (speech)** | **+18.9** | **+14.2** | **+0.74** | **+0.88** | 67% |
| +1 | −17.3 | −22.1 | −0.71 | −0.70 | 48% |
| +2 | +9.0 | +4.2 | +0.22 | +0.46 | 61% |
| +3 | +27.6 | +22.9 | +1.28 | +1.33 | 73% |
| +4 | +14.1 | +9.4 | +0.64 | +1.44 | 61% |
| +5 | +1.0 | −3.7 | −0.18 | +0.05 | 52% |

- **No offset clears the inference bar.** The largest statistic anywhere in the window
  is offset −2 at **HAC *t* = +1.75** (Welch +1.21) — and that is the *maximum over 11
  correlated offsets*, so even it does not survive a multiple-testing eye.
- The **speech day itself** runs **+18.9 bps** mean (HAC *t* = **+0.88**), a 67% win-rate
  — pleasant, but indistinguishable from noise.
- The sign **alternates** offset-to-offset (−1 down, 0 up, +1 down): the hallmark of a
  pattern fit to 33 points, not a structural drift.

## The thin-sample CI — why one-event-a-year can't certify anything

Circular-block-bootstrap (block = 3) 95% CI on the **speech-day** mean return:

| statistic | value |
|---|--:|
| speech-day mean | +18.9 bps |
| 95% CI (block bootstrap) | **[−17.6 bps, +60.6 bps]** |

The interval **straddles zero** by a wide margin. With one observation per year, 33
years buys ~33 events; the standard error is large enough that a +19 bps point estimate
is fully consistent with no effect.

## The only traded arm — react to the speech (long the next session)

Long SPY from the **speech-day close** for `hold` sessions (one execution lag: the
reaction trade earns the *next* session's return), one trade per year, costs 1 bp one-way
charged on entry and exit (round-trip = 2 bp), net:

| hold (sessions) | n | win-rate | mean (bps/trade) | per-trade Sharpe | HAC *t* |
|---:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 1 | 33 | 45% | **−19.3** | −0.11 | −0.78 |
| 2 | 33 | 58% | −11.4 | −0.07 | −0.55 |
| 3 | 33 | 64% | +16.0 | +0.09 | +0.51 |

Reacting to the speech is a coin flip with a fee: the 1-session arm is **negative** net,
none of the holds clears |*t*| = 0.8. There is nothing here to trade.

## Synthetic positive control — the engine is a faithful detector

On the deterministic synthetic tape the same event machinery recovers a planted
speech-day bump and finds nothing in the null:

| tape | planted speech-day bump | speech-day HAC *t* | detected? |
|---|--:|--:|:--:|
| Null (`bump = 0`) | 0 bps | +0.36 | no (correct) |
| Positive control (`bump = 0.008`) | +80 bps | +4.13 | yes |

The harness banks a real planted effect at *t* = +4.13 and stays quiet on the null — so
the flat real-tape result is a statement about **the market**, not a dead pipeline.

## Verdict

- **Signal — NONE.** No session offset around the Jackson Hole keynote clears the
  inference bar; the strongest statistic anywhere in the −5…+5 window is HAC *t* = +1.75
  (and that is the max over 11 correlated offsets). The speech-day mean's 95% CI is
  [−17.6, +60.6] bps — squarely across zero. The alternating sign is curve-fitting on 33
  points, not a drift.
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** The literal "react to the speech" trade is **net negative**
  at a one-session hold (−19.3 bps, *t* = −0.78) and never significant at any hold. One
  event a year caps capacity at ~31 round trips per career; there is no edge to scale.
- **A "Jackson Hole drift"? — NOT SUPPORTED.** A handful of memorable keynotes
  (Bernanke 2010, Powell 2022) seeded a folk belief in a calendar drift the full 33-year
  record does not carry. Salient anecdotes, not a signal.
